tasks.q: What does a trace table record?
a: The value of each variable as the program runs, and anything it outputs
Which language it is written in
tasks.fb: It is a picture of the program's state, step by step.

tasks.q: Why is it useful for finding logic errors?
a: It shows exactly which line the values first go wrong on
tasks.fb: You compare what the values are with what they should be.

tasks.q: Trace this program and complete the table.
tasks.fb: The total runs 0, 1, 3, 6, and the output happens after the loop finishes.
tasks.title: Trace: adding 1 to 3

tasks.q: Why only write a value when it changes?
a: It keeps the table readable and shows clearly where each change happened
tasks.fb: A column of repeated numbers hides what matters.

tasks.q: Trace this program and complete the table.
tasks.fb: 20 halves to 10, 5, 2 then 1, so the loop runs four times.
tasks.title: Trace: halving until one

tasks.q: A while loop's condition is false the first time it is tested. How many rows does the loop add?
tasks.fb: A while loop may run zero times; a do-until always runs at least once.

tasks.q: Trace this program with a mark of 62 and complete the table.
tasks.fb: 62 fails the first test and passes the second, so grade becomes M.
tasks.title: Trace: the grade program

tasks.q: In an if-elseif-else, how many branches run?
tasks.fb: The first condition that is true wins, and the rest are skipped.

stations.name: Finding the bug with a trace

tasks.q: This program should output the largest of the three numbers. Trace it and complete the table.
code: if b > largest then largest = b
if c > largest then largest = c
tasks.fb: largest starts at 4, becomes 9, and 2 does not beat it.
tasks.title: Trace: the largest of three

tasks.q: Your trace shows the right values until line 6, where total becomes 12 instead of 10. What does that tell you?
tasks.fb: The first divergence locates the fault.

tasks.q: Trace this program and complete the table.
tasks.fb: x goes 7, 4, 1 then -2, which ends the loop, and y totals 12.
tasks.title: Trace: the final table

tasks.q: Why is it worth tracing carefully rather than guessing the answer?
a: Marks are given for the intermediate values, not just the final output
The final answer carries no marks
tasks.fb: A wrong final answer with a correct trace still scores.

tasks.q: Trace this program, which finds the greatest common divisor of 12 and 8.
code: if a > b then a = a - b
tasks.fb: 12 minus 8 gives 4; then 8 minus 4 gives 4; a and b are equal, so the loop ends.
tasks.title: Trace: greatest common divisor

info.title: Also called a dry run
info.text: Running a program in your head with pen and paper is a dry run; the trace table is where you write it down.

info.title: Before debuggers
info.text: Early programmers had no way to inspect a running program, so tracing by hand was the only debugging technique there was.

info.title: Still used
info.text: Professional programmers still trace tricky loops by hand, because a debugger shows what happens and a trace shows why.

info.title: Watch the loop condition
info.text: Most trace table mistakes come from going round a loop one time too many or too few. Check the condition every time.

info.title: Output is not a variable
info.text: A common exam error is writing the output in a variable column. Give it a column of its own.

info.title: Exam tip
info.text: If a table has six rows printed, the examiner expects six rows used. An unused row is a hint that you stopped too early.
